subject: Dedicated sizing + technical deep dive — Nimbus Analytics
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@nimbusanalytics.com>, Tim Luo <tim.luo@nimbusanalytics.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated sizing + technical deep dive — Nimbus Analytics

Hi Lena / Tim —

Thanks again for the discovery call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Goal: Dedicated pool for low-latency real-time scoring of candidate models (vision + text combo). You mentioned ~800 concurrent requests at peak and a target p95 end-to-end inference latency < 120ms.
- Primary constraint: model KV cache hit rate is variable; some calls include longer context windows (~2k tokens) during peak batch operations.
- Key success criteria for the sizing call: agree on expected request profile, confirm acceptable SLOs, and map to an initial Dedicated pool config (GPU type + instance count + burst).

Proposed next step: 45–60 minute technical deep dive / dedicated sizing call where we bring tooling to estimate throughput and propose a starting footprint. Suggested slots (PST):
  • Tue Nov 23 — 10:00–11:00
  • Wed Nov 24 — 09:00–10:00

Ask before the call (if available):
  - sample 24h traffic matrix (per-minute or per-5min),
  - p50/p95/p99 latency targets,
  - an example payload size distribution and average token lengths,
  - whether you use persistent KV cache across sessions.

If those two slots don't work, send 2–3 alternatives and we’ll align. I’ll follow up with an invite once we lock time. I’ve looped Alex (solutions) and Jonas (inference) to join the sizing session.

Thanks —
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai
redwood.ai

Thanks for the clear summary. Wed Nov 24 09:00–10:00 PST works best for our team. We’ll plan for 3 folks from Nimbus: myself, Tim (technical lead), and Maya Patel (infra).

I’ll attach a short traffic extract and the current p95/p99 numbers — see attached: nimbus_throughput_summary.xlsx. That should give you a sense of bursts vs baseline.

Can you confirm whether you need sample model binaries or is a payload-level example sufficient for the first sizing run?

Appreciate it —

Thanks — locking Nov 24 09:00 PST on my calendar. I’ll prepare the Dedicated pool baseline (GPU choices + expected token throughput) and bring the config checklist so we can run numbers live.

I’ve attached the latest pricing/packaging doc we discussed for quick reference: redwood_pricing_v2.pdf. Please don’t share the internal notes externally.

Hi Lena / Tim —

Great — we’re confirmed for Wed Nov 24, 09:00–10:00 PST. I just sent a calendar invite (Google) with the video link.

Lena: payload-level examples are fine for the first pass. If you can share a sample model signature (inputs/outputs) or an export of a single inference payload that includes token counts that’d be even better, but not required. The traffic extract you attached is perfect to start.

I’ve added a short pre-call checklist to the Drive folder and attached a copy here as well: technical_precall_checklist.docx — it includes the minimal fields our sizing script needs.

Agenda (30–45 min):
  1) Quick alignment on traffic profile and SLOs (10m)
  2) Live sizing run with sample payloads (20–25m)
  3) Recommendation and next steps (5–10m)

See you Wednesday —
